subject: Hosted API token pricing & rate protection — BrightPath commit discussion
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@brightpath.ai
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API pricing / committed tiers question

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — BrightPath is excited about the latency profile on the Redwood hosted API. We're getting internal alignment around budget and procurement and I wanted to loop in contracts up front so we can move quickly. Two quick asks: 

1) Can you share a simple committed-tier pricing schedule (per-token) for hosted usage? Our expected steady-state is ~1.2B tokens/month for generation + 200M embeddings.
2) We need clarity on rate protections: price locks for the contract term, and whether Redwood will accept an MFN clause or a CPI-based cap on annual price increases.

Attached is an initial SOW for context (BrightPath_SOW_v1.pdf).

Elena
Director of Platform Product
BrightPath Analytics

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, contracts@brightpath.ai
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / committed tiers question

Elena — thanks for the SOW and the clear asks. Re: committed tiers and rate protections, I outlined two paths below that mirror what we've done for similar customers. I've attached a simple pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid.csv) to make the math easier.

Short version (options):

A) Standard commit (12 months) — volume tiers with per-token step-downs
  - 0–500M tokens/month: $0.0020 per token
  - 500M–1.5B tokens/month: $0.0016 per token
  - >1.5B tokens/month: $0.0013 per token
  - Embeddings: flat $0.0008 per unit at >200M/month
  - Price lock: 12 months for the agreed per-token rates above (no increases during term)

B) High-commit (24 months) — deeper discounts, conditional on minimum monthly commits
  - 0–500M: $0.0018
  - 500M–1.5B: $0.0014
  - >1.5B: $0.0011
  - Embeddings: $0.0007
  - Price lock: 24 months

Rate-protection items we commonly handle:
  - Price lock for the term (we can commit in contract language).
  - MFN: we are cautious about MFN across public commercial offers; we can offer MFN for deals with comparable commit/term and usage profile but need carveouts for promotional/public pricing and channel/partner co-sell arrangements.
  - CPI cap: we can agree to an annual CPI-linked increase cap, typical range 3–5% depending on term. For 12-months we usually set 3%; for 24-months we can go up to 4%.

If BrightPath needs more stringent MFN language (e.g., across all public customers), that typically requires legal to negotiate and may affect pricing.

Next steps: I can send a short commit proposal that spells this out and includes an Exhibit A with exact tier math. Rishi is looped for deal structure and legal cadence.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

From: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.ai>

Cc: BrightPath Contracts <contracts@brightpath.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 14:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / committed tiers question

Thanks Sean — that helps. A few clarifications from our side before legal takes a formal review:

- BrightPath is targeting the High-commit path but wants a 12-month ramp to reach >=1.2B tokens/month. We'd propose MMR (minimum monthly run-rate) that steps up over Q1/Q2.
- On MFN: we cannot accept broad promotional carveouts. Our procurement team is asking if we can get a true MFN for the same commit/term structure (i.e., if Redwood offers a lower published price to another customer with comparable throughput and committed spend, BrightPath gets parity).
- On CPI cap: our budget model assumes no more than 3% YoY increases; would Redwood accept a firm 3% annual cap for a 24-month contract if we take the High-commit pricing?

If you can put these items in writing we can share with our GC and contracts. Also — please include any explicit exclusions (e.g., credits, promotional pilots) so we know what's carved out.

Elena

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@brightpath.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, BrightPath Contracts <contracts@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / committed tiers question

Hi Elena — Rishi here (Sales Lead). Appreciate the clear feedback. We can do a pragmatic compromise that gets you predictable unit economics while protecting Redwood's ability to price competitively for different deal shapes. Key points in the attached proposal (RP-commit-proposal-20260504.pdf):

1) Commit & ramp: 24-month agreement with a defined 3-month ramp that scales to your target of 1.2B tokens/month by Month 4, then a firm MMR thereafter. Exhibit A has the per-month ramp schedule.

2) Price lock: committed per-token rates fixed for the first 12 months. After Month 12, the published rates can change annually but increases are capped at 4% YoY.

3) MFN: we will accept an MFN limited to deals that meet all of the following: (a) same commit duration, (b) same or higher guaranteed monthly run-rate, and (c) not driven by promotional or limited pilot credits. This language narrows MFN to comparable commercial deals. 

4) CPI vs fixed cap: instead of CPI linkage, we propose a fixed 4% cap (as above) for predictability. For customers who strongly prefer CPI linkage, we are open to a CPI-based cap with a floor/ceiling (e.g., min 0%, max 5%) — that requires explicit legal review.

5) Public promotions & channel deals: we will carve out limited-time public promotions and partner channel co-sells where pricing is set by a partner program. We will document specific exclusions in the contract.

6) Legal and timelines: if this is acceptable in principle, our commercial counsel will prepare a redline for BrightPath's GC. We can target an internal sign-off and DocuSign routing within 10 business days once language is agreed.

I've attached the proposal (RP-commit-proposal-20260504.pdf) and included the pricing grid for clarity. Sean will coordinate next steps on implementation items (billing, routing rules, observability permissions).

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

On a separate note, Marcus — can you confirm the readiness of the dedicated token-metering export for BrightPath? We should provide an SFTP or API hook for usage reporting as part of the contract.
